items.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
items.q: The interviewee mentions Joe Howard in the context of teaching the interviewer's son ('Joe Howard taught him a couple of months') and the interviewer confirms knowledge of Joe Howard ('He said he used to be a fine trumpet player'). There is no evidence the interviewee personally knew, met, or collab

ctx.x: What is it? Well, I'll tell you that. Can you tell us any more about your son, and we didn't talk too much about him? That's his girlfriend. How old was he when he started to play? Do you remember? He can't go far with you, but that's her girlfriend.

Oh, as soon as his dad got his son. Her girlfriend, yes. He started to do music. Yes. And Joe Howard taught him a couple of months, and that was all. I got to graduate in graduate school. I used to teach him before I became a supervisor. He was 14. He wasn't quite 14 when he was daddy. And during that spring, he started to take the music. He didn't study with his father then at all? No, not with his father at all. Uh-uh, not with his father at all. But Joe Howard started. Joe. It was then Joe. Oh, man. You…

and I played bass. Oh, man, Joe Howard. Yeah, Joe Howard. He's a criminalized devil. Yeah, uh-huh. He's a good musician. He's a good big brother. But you hear that? Oh, man. Oh, yeah. He was a bug-looser together. Do a depression job. You know, if you're a... A little cute. A fine man. Yeah.
